objective: Report repeat customers. `stockroom/report.py` gets `repeat_customers(book: OrderBook) -> list[str]`: the names of the customers who have ordered more than once, each name once, sorted in plain string order. Customers are told apart by the exact `customer` text of their orders. A new command `python -m stockroom repeat-customers --orders FILE` reads an order file, prints the names one per line in that order, or the single line `no repeat customers` when there are none, and exits with code 0.
acceptance: `repeat_customers` lists a customer with several ordinary orders once, leaves out customers with a single order, sorts in plain string order (`Ada`, `Zed`, `adam`) and is `[]` for an empty book
Names that differ in capitalization or in a trailing space are different customers
A customer who has other orders besides a cancelled one is still listed when those other orders alone are several (`Ivo` with a paid, a cancelled and an open order)
For the sample orders the list contains `Hana Kim` and `Omar Diaz` and is sorted
`repeat-customers` prints the names one per line in the same order, or `no repeat customers`, exits with 0 and writes nothing to stderr
A customer whose orders include cancelled ones is listed or left out by the rule that the customer ordered more than once

interpretations: Every order the customer placed counts, cancelled ones included: a paid order plus a cancelled order make a repeat customer
Only orders that are not cancelled count, as in the revenue figures: a paid order plus a cancelled order is a single order
